points: Site: **plantar** metatarsal heads, heel, tips of toes, under bunions.
Deep, punched-out, surrounded by **callus**; may reach bone.
Often **painless**; warm foot with good pulses (unless neuro-ischaemic).
Clawed toes, Charcot deformity, dry fissured skin.
, plus X-ray or MRI if osteomyelitis is suspected.
Test sensation with a **10 g monofilament** and vibration.
Deep tissue samples rather than surface swabs if infected.

items.t: Diabetic foot with **spreading redness, fever, crepitus or wet necrosis**: **ED / same-day admission**.
Probe to bone, or suspected osteomyelitis or **Charcot foot** (hot, swollen foot in neuropathy).
**Never ignore a ‘small’ plantar ulcer in diabetes.**

pearls.t: Teach **daily foot checks**, sensible footwear and podiatry follow-up; never walk barefoot with neuropathy.
Painless ulcer under a callus suggests neuropathic.

quiz.q: Name a red flag that needs escalation.
quiz.a: Diabetic foot with **spreading redness, fever, crepitus or wet necrosis**: **ED / same-day admission**.
